correctness.rationale: Exact star binomial cluster count and path open-run enumeration yield tail polynomials. Binomial-basis decomposition gives exact conditional coefficients. The conditional path/star risk ratios are strictly log-concave; coefficient signs are positive then negative, with a sharp boundary from the next-to-last coefficient [t(t-1)-(n-1)]/[n(n-1)]. Dividing by the first negative Bernstein basis function gives a strictly decreasing quotient, proving the unique transverse parameter crossing and strict ordering on either side. The mean comparison is independently a sum of ordered-pair distance powers. Exact rational code rechecks finite instances and identities; all unbounded quantifiers rest on the written analytical proof.

value.rationale: This is a sharp all-parameter classification of a genuine risk-measure reversal between two canonical sparse-contact network structures. One topology strictly maximizes average component size yet loses for upper-tail risks once the population exceeds t(t-1)+1 and transmissibility crosses a unique point. The integer population cutoff and first n=8 example are motivated structural boundaries, not cherry-picked numerical slices. The mean comparison is acknowledged as prior context; the unique-crossing theorem, monotonicity proof and sharp dimension/threshold cutoff add distinct value.
